requirements.requirement: Usable live native credentials for real Kimi JSON/SSE rather than a retained token snapshot
requirements.implementation: New public KimiCodingOAuthProvider/Config and KimiCodingOAuthCredentialSource retain the explicit native resolver. Frozen issuer/normalized effective headers and captured endpoint/provider/model fence the operation. The facade discards supplied API keys, resolves only valid fresh matching native Kimi credentials before transport and revalidates the local grant after I/O. It creates a per-operation existing KimiCodingProvider with actual Bearer, so simultaneous turns do not mutate a shared key. The four original profiles/prices/output/thinking/tools/JSON-SSE codecs remain unchanged. Model/output/image validation precedes credential resolution; empty model override retains the old configured-model fallback.
requirements.proof: Two new JSON/SSE journeys use actual native request bodies/headers and the existing pinned continuation fixture. Fresh token/same-grant restart/replay retains exact vendor signatures without the harness envelope on wire; caller histories remain identical. Wrong/expired/generic/foreign-realm credentials cannot fall through to a supplied key or make inference requests. Invalid model/output/remote-image requests do not call the resolver. Compiled public SDK executes native capture/rotation/replay and post-I/O withdrawal with three mocked requests.

requirements.requirement: Private native grant continuation without key/realm/model/endpoint/header/derived borrowing
requirements.implementation: Reuse the existing gateway scoped-envelope codec with a Kimi-native grant tag and reserved ai-harness:kimi-oauth:v1 signature prefix, not a new replay/session framework. Scope includes exact facade membership, local issuer/grant, requested model/API/provider, endpoint and effective headers; same-grant token rotation is stable. Native envelopes alone unwrap before the existing A codec. The old API-key/explicit-Bearer Kimi path strips only newly introduced prefixed native envelopes to its public foreign projection, never forwarding the wrapper as a raw vendor signature. Existing raw private Kimi behavior stays unchanged. This is structural SDK ownership, not vendor signature authentication or a sandbox against arbitrary in-process JS.
requirements.proof: Both facades capture, append0600 v2 session data, reload and reconstruct a new native SDK instance after token rotation. Changed grant/header/endpoint/model/derived receivers and the legacy API-key lane receive no opaque fields; original history is unchanged. Existing19 owning Kimi cases retain raw/private/profile behavior, and21 gateway cases retain the shared codec/policy controls. No MOD-03 protocol/profile redelivery or new SDK acquisition follows.

requirements.implementation: Resolver waits, delegate I/O and awaited chunk/completion callbacks use caller/scope/request-timeout cancellation. The delegate borrows existing owned-response lifetime via its exact native consumer marker. Scope replacement cannot publish a delayed old resolver; the next generation is reusable. Fixed native errors preserve observed response usage through SpecializedModelError when live authority is withdrawn after I/O. Private tool events are sealed, and raw start/end/done payloads cannot expose private signatures.
requirements.proof: One uncooperative source is retired before any transport by network-scope reset, then a fresh request recovers. One owned inference body is caller-cancelled exactly once without waiting for hostile cancellation or invoking completion. Post-I/O source withdrawal refuses completion, retains observed14-token usage and permits a new request. Initial cancellation tests expose an unobserved outer cancellation promise; it is now observed from the first resolver wait, without weakened tests/flags.
